body.statement: Assume \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\ne\varnothing\). For every \(m\in\mathcal M\), the attainable selected-column subdistributions \(z_w\) are exactly those satisfying \(z_w=0\) for \(w>L_m\), \(0\le z_w\le q_w\), \(\sum_{w=0}^{L_m}z_w=a_m\), and \(\sum_{w=0}^{s}z_w\ge A_s\) for \(0\le s\le L_m\). Their pointwise maximal and minimal cumulative arrays are respectively \(Z_{ms}^{-}\) and \(Z_{ms}^{+}\) from \(\text{def:threshold-cumulative-envelopes}\). In particular, \(Z_{m,L_m}^{-}=Z_{m,L_m}^{+}=a_m\) and \(Z_{ms}^{+}=\max\{A_s,Z_{m,s+1}^{+}-q_{s+1}\}\) for \(s<L_m\). Consequently, \(\inf_{x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)}\sum_{b\ge m,w}w x_{bw}=L_ma_m-\sum_{s=0}^{L_m-1}Z_{ms}^{-}\) and \(\sup_{x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)}\sum_{b\ge m,w}w x_{bw}=L_ma_m-\sum_{s=0}^{L_m-1}Z_{ms}^{+}\), with both endpoints attained. The sharp endpoints for \(J_m\) add \(\pi\sum_{b<m}\mu_b\) and multiply the displayed selected contribution by \(\pi\).
body.justification: Dahl2008, Theorem 4, supplies the attributed feasibility support; the new closed forms expose the backward capacity deficit that unrestricted sum bounds omit and permit exact threshold comparisons without repeated linear programs.
body.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 resolves discrete sharpness for unrestricted fixed-marginal sums; the support deletion \(b+w>H\) changes both feasibility and the upper endpoint through the backward deficit.
body.consumer: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025's fixed-threshold switching loss becomes sharply bounded in an externally prespecified capacity-sensitivity analysis.
